When he submitted in compliance, that rivalry departed and love was purified for its rightful owner. Then the glad tidings came: ﴿And We ransomed him with a tremendous sacrifice﴾.

The intent was not that he should be punished, but that he should be tested so as to be refined.

The wonder is not in the Friend's command to slaughter the son; the wonder is in his carrying out the slaughter with his own hand. Had it not been for total immersion in love of the command, such a command would not have been easy to bear. Therefore its traces were made a place of return for hearts, which yearn for them more intensely than birds yearn for their nests.

(Chapter)

Consider the state of our third father, Ibrahim, the imam of the upright ones (hunafa'), the shaykh of the prophets, the pillar of the world, and the Friend of the Lord of the worlds among the children of Adam.

Consider what his trial led to, his patience, and his giving of himself to God.

Consider how his giving of himself to God and his support of His religion led to God taking him as a khalil for Himself, and commanding His Messenger and Friend Muhammad (ﷺ) to follow his creed. I will point out to you one quality of the many things God honoured him with in his trial of slaughtering his son. God, blessed and exalted, rewarded him for surrendering his son to God's command by blessing his offspring and multiplying them until they filled the plain and the mountain. God, blessed and exalted, is not outdone in generosity by anyone, and He is the most generous of the generous.

Whoever leaves something for His sake, or does something for His sake, God gives him multiples of what he left of that thing, many times over, and rewards him with many times over what he did for His sake. When Ibrahim was commanded to slaughter his son, he hastened to obey God's command, and the son agreed with his father, out of mutual contentment and submission. God, knowing their truthfulness and fidelity, ransomed him with a tremendous sacrifice and gave them what He gave them of His bounty. Among some of His gifts was that He blessed their descendants until they filled the earth, for the purpose of having children is nothing but procreation and the multiplication of offspring. For this reason Ibrahim said: ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from the righteous﴾, and said: ﴿My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [also] from my descendants﴾.

The utmost of what he feared and dreaded from slaughtering his son was the cutting off of his line. When he gave his son to God, and the son gave himself, God multiplied his offspring for him, blessed them, and increased them until they filled the world, and He placed prophethood and the Book among his descendants exclusively, and brought forth from them Muhammad. It is mentioned that Dawud (peace be upon him) wished to know the number of the Children of Israel, so he commanded that they be brought together, and sent for that nuqaba' (leaders) and 'urafa' (overseers), and ordered them to report the count to him. They remained for a period unable to accomplish that. Then God revealed to Dawud: "You know that I promised your father Ibrahim, when he was commanded to slaughter his son and hastened to obey My command, that I would bless his descendants until they become equal to the stars. Make them such that their number cannot be counted. You wish to count a number that I have decreed cannot be counted." He mentioned the rest of the hadith. Thus He made from his line these two great nations whose number none can count but God, their Creator and Provider: the Children of Israel and the Children of Isma'il. Apart from this, God honoured him with the elevation of his mention and beautiful praise, on the tongues of all nations, and among the angels in the heavens. This is part of the fruit of his dealing with God. So woe to the one who knows Him and then deals with others: how losing his bargain is, and how great his regret.

[Section: The Perfection of Love]

Then khullah includes the perfection and ultimate end of love, such that no room remains in the heart for anything other than the beloved. It is a station that does not accept sharing in any way. This station is specific to the two Friends, may the prayers and peace of God be upon them both: Ibrahim and Muhammad, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "God has taken me as a khalil just as He took Ibrahim as a khalil."

In the Sahih, from him (ﷺ), he said: "If I were to take a khalil from among the people of the earth, I would have taken Abu Bakr as a khalil, but your companion is the khalil of God."

In another hadith: "I disavow before every khalil his khullah."

When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) asked for a child and was given one, and his love was attached to his heart, a branch was taken from it. The Beloved was jealous over His khalil that there should be a place in his heart for another, so He commanded him to slaughter him. The command was in a dream, so that carrying out the command would be a greater trial and test. The intent was not the slaughter of the child, but the slaughter of him from the heart, so that the heart would be purified for the Lord. When the Friend (peace be upon him) hastened to comply and placed the love of God above the love of his son, the aim was achieved, the slaughter was lifted, and he was ransomed with a tremendous sacrifice. For the Lord, exalted, never commanded something and then utterly annulled it; rather, He must leave some part of it or a substitute for it, just as He left the law of ransom, and just as He left the recommendation of charity before private conversation, and just as He left the five prayers after the fifty were removed and kept their reward, saying: "The word is not changed before Me: they are five in action and fifty in reward."

[Section: Love and Khullah]

As for what some of the confused think, that love is more perfect than khullah, and that Ibrahim is the khalil of God while Muhammad is the beloved of God, this is from their ignorance. For love is general and khullah is specific, and khullah is the ultimate end of love. The Prophet (ﷺ) informed that God took him as a khalil just as He took Ibrahim as a khalil, and he denied that he could have a khalil other than his Lord, while he informed of his love for Aisha, her father, Umar ibn al-Khattab, and others.

Also, God, glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed, God loves those who are constantly repentant and loves those who purify themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 222]. And ﴿God loves the patient﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 146]. And ﴿God loves the doers of good﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 148]. And ﴿God loves those who act justly﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 42]. The young repentant one is a beloved of God, but khullah is specific to the two Friends. This is only from a lack of knowledge and understanding of God and His Messenger (ﷺ).

(Chapter)

Khullah is the love that penetrates the spirit and heart of the lover until no place remains in it for anything other than the beloved, as it has been said:

"You have penetrated the path of the spirit within me, and for this the intimate friend was named khalil."

This is the secret for which—and God knows best—the Friend was commanded to slaughter his son, the fruit of his heart and the morsel of his liver. For when he asked for a son and was given one, a branch of his heart became attached to him. Khullah is a station that does not accept partnership or division. So the Friend was jealous over his khalil that there should be a place in his heart for another. He therefore commanded him to slaughter the son, to remove the rival from his heart.

When he prepared himself for that and resolved upon it with a firm resolve, the purpose of the command was achieved. There was no benefit left in taking the son's life, so He prevented it and ransomed him with a tremendous sacrifice. He was told: ﴿O Ibrahim, you have fulfilled the vision﴾ [al-Saffat: 104], that is, you acted as one who affirms it. ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good﴾ [al-Saffat: 80], We reward whoever hastens to obey Us, so We gladden his eye just as We gladdened your eye by your compliance with Our commands, and by preserving the son and his safety. ﴿Indeed, this was the clear trial﴾ [al-Saffat: 106]: it is the Beloved's testing of His lover, and His examining him so that he prefers His pleasure. Thus He perfects His blessings upon him; it is a trial of affliction and a gift of grace upon him together.

This call, to which only the special ones of His creation are summoned, and among them the people of intellect and insight, is not answered by everyone. Not every eye is comforted by it. Its people are those who are in the midst of the right hand's grasp on the day of the two graspings, and the rest of the people of the right hand are at its edges.

"Not every eye is comforted by the Beloved, nor does everyone who is called answer the caller."

"Whoever does not answer the caller of your guidance, leave him; he will answer everyone who has become a caller to error."

"And say to the inflamed eyes: beware of seeing the light of the sun, so cover yourself against the darkness of the nights."

"And forgive souls that did not give themselves to their beloved; leave them and what they chose, and do not be harsh."

[Section: The Drowning]

The Shaykh al-Islam said:

(Chapter of Drowning) God Most High said: ﴿So when they had both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead﴾ [al-Saffat: 103].

This is a term by which, in this chapter, is indicated one who has reached the middle of the station and passed the limit of separation.

The manner of his inference from the indication of the verse: when Ibrahim (ﷺ) and his son reached what they reached in hastening to comply and resolving to carry out the slaughter commanded, the father laid him upon his forehead at once, took the knife and swung it toward his throat. In that state he turned away from himself and his son, and passed away by God's command from them both. Thus he entered the sea of gathering of secret, heart, and concern upon God, and passed the limit of distinction that prevents compliance with this command.

His words: "﴿When they had both submitted﴾" means they surrendered and yielded to God's command, so there remained no dispute from either the father or the son, but pure submission and complete surrender.

His words: "﴿and he put him down upon his forehead﴾" means he threw him down upon his forehead, which is the side of the brow that faces the ground when one lies down, and that is the posture of one who is to be slaughtered.

His words: "he reached the middle of the station" he does not mean a specific station, and for this reason he left it indefinite and did not restrict it. The "station" among them is a stage of the stations of the wayfarers, and it differs according to its levels, and it has a beginning, a middle, and an end. The "drowning" referred to is to become in the middle of the station.

If it is said: drowning is more specific to the end of the station than to its middle, because it is immersion in it, such that it engulfs the heart and concern, so how does the Shaykh make it a middle in it?

I say: when the seeker's aspiration in this state is gathered upon the aim, and he turns away from all else, he has departed from the station of distinction and passed its limit into the station of gathering. He begins within the station, and the beginning of every station resembles the end of the one before it. When he reaches the middle of it, it engulfs his heart, concern, and will, just as one drowns who reaches the middle of a deep sea before arriving at its far shore.

(Section: That the Sacrifice Was Isma'il (peace be upon him))

Isma'il is the one who was sacrificed according to the correct view of the scholars among the Companions, the Successors, and those after them.

As for the claim that it was Ishaq, it is false for more than twenty reasons. I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya—may God sanctify his spirit—say: this view is only taken from the People of the Book, and it is even false by the text of their own book. For in it: God commanded Ibrahim to slaughter his son, his firstborn, and in one wording: his only son. The People of the Book, along with the Muslims, do not doubt that Isma'il is his firstborn. What deceived the proponents of this view is that in the Torah in their hands is: "Slaughter your son Ishaq." He said: this addition is from their distortion and lying, for it contradicts His saying: "Slaughter your firstborn and your only one." But the Jews envied the sons of Isma'il this honour and wished it to be theirs, and to bring it to themselves and claim it for themselves apart from the Arabs. But God refuses except to make His favour belong to its people. How could it be said that the sacrificed one was Ishaq, when God gave glad tidings to Ishaq's mother of him and of his son Ya'qub? God Most High said, speaking of the angels, that they said to Ibrahim when they brought him the glad tidings: ﴿Do not fear, for we have been sent to the people of Lut.—And his wife was standing, and she laughed, and We gave her glad tidings of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾ [Hud: 70–71]. It is impossible that He should give her the glad tidings that a child will be born to her and then command that he be slaughtered. And there is no doubt that Ya'qub (may God be pleased with him) is included in the glad tidings, so the glad tidings include Ishaq and Ya'qub in one wording, and this is the apparent meaning of the speech and its context.

If it is said: had the matter been as you have mentioned, "Ya'qub" would have been in the genitive as a conjunction with Ishaq, and the reading would be ﴿and after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾, that is, "and Ya'qub from after Ishaq".

It is said: the nominative does not prevent Ya'qub from being the one given glad tidings, because glad tidings are a specific speech, and it is the first true joyful report.

God's words: ﴿and after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾ [Hud: 71] is a sentence that includes these conditions, so it is glad tidings; indeed, the true reality of glad tidings is the declarative sentence.

And since glad tidings are speech, the position of this sentence is in the accusative by way of reporting after a verb of saying, as if the meaning is: "and We said to her: after Ishaq, Ya'qub." And the speaker, when he says, "I gave so-and-so glad tidings of the arrival of his brother and his family behind him," is understood by no one except as giving glad tidings of both matters together. This is what no person of understanding doubts at all. Then another matter weakens the genitive reading: the weakness of your saying, "I passed by Zayd and after him 'Amr," and because the conjunction stands in the place of the preposition, so it is not separated from the genitive, just as the preposition is not separated from the genitive.

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary on Surah 37, verses 102–107 (part 2 of 2):

And it is also indicated by the fact that when Allah, glorified is He, mentioned the story of Ibrahim and his son, the one who was sacrificed, in Surah (al-Saffat), He said: ﴿So when they both had submitted, and he put him down upon his forehead, And We called to him, "O Ibrahim, You have fulfilled the vision." Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good. Indeed, this was the clear trial. And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice. And We left for him among later generations: "Peace upon Ibrahim." Thus do We reward the doers of good. Indeed, he was among Our believing servants.﴾ [al-Saffat: 103–111].

Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿And We gave him the good news of Ishaq, a prophet from among the righteous.﴾ [al-Saffat: 112]. This is a good news from Allah, exalted is He, to him, as a reward for his patience in what he was commanded. This is very clear that the one given the good news of was other than the first, rather it is almost explicit in that.

If it is said: The second good news was about his prophethood, meaning that when the father was patient in what he was commanded, and the son submitted to the command of Allah, Allah rewarded him for that by granting him prophethood.

It is said: The good news was given regarding the whole: his very person and existence, and that he would be a prophet. That is why "nabiyyan" is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal muqaddar), meaning: "destined to be a prophet." So it is not possible to take the good news as referring to the essence and then restrict it to a subordinate circumstantial clause that functions like an adjunct; this is an absurd way of speaking. Rather, when the good news concerns his prophethood, then its concerning his existence is more fitting and more appropriate.

Also, there is no doubt that the one sacrificed was in Makkah, which is why the sacrifices on the day of sacrifice (yawm al-nahr) are performed there, just as the sa'i between al-Safa and al-Marwa and the stoning of the pillars (rami al-jimar) were prescribed as a reminder of the matter of Isma'il and his mother, and to keep alive the remembrance of Allah. It is well known that Isma'il and his mother were the ones who were in Makkah, not Ishaq and his mother. For this reason, the place and time of the sacrifice are connected to the Sacred House (al-Bayt al-Haram), whose building was shared by Ibrahim and Isma'il, and slaughtering in Makkah was part of the completion of the Hajj to the House, which was established by the hand of Ibrahim and his son Isma'il, in time and place. Had the sacrifice been in al-Sham, as the People of the Book claim and those who took from them maintain, then the sacrifices and the slaughter would have been in al-Sham and not in Makkah.

Also, Allah, glorified is He, named the one sacrificed "Halim" (forbearing), because none is more forbearing than one who submits himself to slaughter in obedience to his Lord. And when He mentioned Ishaq, He named him "'Alim" (knowing). He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Has there come to you the story of the honored guests of Ibrahim? When they entered upon him and said, "Peace." He said, "Peace, a people unknown."﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 24–25]

Up to His saying: ﴿They said, "Do not fear," and gave him good tidings of a knowing boy.﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 28]

This is Ishaq without doubt, because he was from his wife, and she was the one who was given the good news of him. As for Isma'il, he was from the concubine (suriyyah). Also, both of them were given the good news of him in old age and despair of having a child, whereas Isma'il was born before that.

Also, Allah, glorified is He, established the human custom that the firstborn is more beloved to the parents than those born after him. When Ibrahim, peace be upon him, asked his Lord for a child and He granted him one, a portion of his heart became attached to love for him. And Allah, exalted is He, had taken him as a close friend (khalil), and friendship (khullah) is a station that requires the singling out of the Beloved with love, and that no one else be made to share in it. So when the son took a portion of the father's heart, the jealousy of the friendship came to pull it out of the heart of the Khalil. So He commanded him to sacrifice the beloved. When he proceeded to sacrifice him, and the love of Allah was greater in his heart than the love of the son, the friendship was then purified of any admixture of partnership. Thus there remained no benefit in the slaughter, since the benefit lay in the resolve and the settling of the soul upon it. The purpose had been achieved, so the command was abrogated, the sacrificial son was ransomed, the Khalil confirmed the vision, and the Lord's objective was fulfilled.

It is known that this trial and test occurred with the first-born only, and it would not have occurred with another child apart from the first. Rather, in the other child there was no competition with the friendship that would call for a command to slaughter him. This is most evident.

Also, Sarah, the wife of the Khalil (ﷺ), was extremely jealous of Hajar and her son, for she was a slave-girl. When she bore Isma'il and his father loved him, Sarah's jealousy intensified, so Allah, glorified is He, commanded that Hajar and her son be taken away from her and settled in the land of Makkah, so that the heat of jealousy would cool from Sarah. This was from His mercy and compassion, exalted is He. How then would He command, after this, that her son be slaughtered while the son of the slave-girl is left as he is? This is with Allah's mercy toward her, the removal of harm from her, and His restoring her. How then would He command, after this, the slaughter of her son rather than the son of the slave-girl? Rather, His perfect wisdom required that He command the slaughter of the son of the concubine, so that the heart of the mistress would soften toward her and her son, and the harshness of jealousy would turn into mercy, and the blessing of this slave-girl and her son would become manifest to her, and that Allah does not waste a household of which this woman and her son are part. And so that He might show His servants His restoring after breaking, His gentleness after hardship, and that the outcome of the patience of Hajar and her son in distance, loneliness, strangeness and submission to the slaughter of the son, led to what it led to: making their traces and footsteps rites for His believing servants and acts of worship for them until the Day of Resurrection. This is His sunnah, exalted is He, toward whomever He wills to elevate among His creation: that He bestows favor upon him after his weakness, humiliation and brokenness. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We wished to confer favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them the inheritors.﴾ [al-Qasas: 5]

That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.

(Section)

And he said in Ighathat al-Lahfan, quoting Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah in his book "al-Jawab al-Sahih liman Baddala Din al-Masih":

He said: In their Torah, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, said to Ibrahim, peace be upon him: "Sacrifice your son, your firstborn, your only one, Ishaq," an addition by them to the wording of the Torah.

I say: This is definitively false from ten aspects.

The first: his firstborn and only son is Isma'il, by the consensus of the three faiths. So combining that he was commanded to sacrifice his firstborn with specifying him as Ishaq is combining two contradictories.

The second: Allah, glorified and exalted is He, commanded Ibrahim to move Hajar and her son Isma'il away from Sarah and settle them in the wilderness of Makkah, lest Sarah be upset. So He commanded the removal of the concubine and her son from her, preserving her heart and averting the harm of jealousy from her. How then would He, glorified and exalted is He, after this command the slaughter of Sarah's son and leave the concubine's son? This is something wisdom does not require.

The third: the story of the sacrifice was certainly in Makkah, and for this reason Allah made the slaughter of offerings and sacrifices in Makkah, as a reminder to the community of what happened between their father Ibrahim and his son.

The fourth: Allah, glorified is He, gave Sarah, mother of Ishaq, the good news: ﴿of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾ [Hud: 71]. So He gave her the good news of both together. How then would He, after that, command the slaughter of Ishaq, when He had given their parents the good news of the child of his child?

The fifth: when Allah, glorified and exalted is He, mentioned the story of the one sacrificed, and his surrender of himself to Allah, and Ibrahim's proceeding to sacrifice him, and finished his story, He said after it:
﴿And We gave him the good news of Ishaq, a prophet from among the righteous.﴾ [al-Saffat: 112].
So Allah gave thanks for his submission to His command and his offering of his son to Him, and made among his reward for that that He gave him Ishaq. Thus Isma'il was saved from the slaughter, and Ishaq was added to him.

The sixth: Ibrahim, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, asked his Lord for a child. Allah answered his supplication and gave him the good news, and when the boy reached the age of striving with him, He commanded him to sacrifice him. He said, exalted is He:
﴿And he said, "Indeed, I will go to my Lord; He will guide me. My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous." So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy.﴾ [al-Saffat: 99–101].
This is evidence that this child was given the good news after his supplication and his asking his Lord to grant him a child, and this one given the good news of is certainly the one commanded to be sacrificed, by the explicit text of the Qur'an.

As for Ishaq, he was given the good news without any supplication from him, rather in old age, and when someone like him could not have a child, and the good news of him was given to his wife Sarah. For this reason she marvelled at the birth of a child from her and him.

He said, exalted is He: ﴿And our messengers did come to Ibrahim with good tidings. They said, "Peace." He said, "Peace," and he did not delay to bring a roasted calf. But when he saw their hands not reaching toward it, he regarded them with suspicion and felt from them fear. They said, "Fear not; indeed, we have been sent to the people of Lut." And his wife was standing, and she laughed, so We gave her good tidings of Ishaq and after Ishaq, Ya'qub. She said, "Oh, woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and this, my husband, is an old man? Indeed, this is an amazing thing." They said, "Are you amazed at the command of Allah?"﴾

So reflect on the context of this good news and that, and you will find them to be two different good tidings, with different origins, one distinct from the other.

The first good news was to him. The second was to her.

The first good news is the one in which the one to be sacrificed was given the good news of, not the second.

The seventh: Ibrahim, peace be upon him, never brought Ishaq to Makkah at all, nor did he separate him from his mother. And how would Allah command him to take the son of his wife, to sacrifice him in the place of his co-wife in her land, and leave the son of his co-wife?

The eighth: when Allah took Ibrahim as a Khalil, friendship implies that his entire heart be attached to his Lord, with no portion of it left for another. When he asked for a child, He gave him Isma'il, and a portion of his heart became attached to him. So His Khalil, glorified is He, wanted that portion to be for Him alone, not for any other creature. So He tested him by commanding the slaughter of his son. When he proceeded to comply, that friendship was purified for Him, and became purely for Allah alone. So the command to slaughter was abrogated, since the purpose had been achieved, which was the resolve and the settling of the soul upon compliance.

It is known that this occurs with the firstborn, not with the last. When this purpose was achieved from the first child, there was no need for the same in the other child. For if the love of the other child had competed with the friendship, he would have been commanded to slaughter him as he commanded the first. And if the one commanded to be slaughtered had been the other child, then He would have permitted him, with the first, to compete with the friendship for a long period, and then commanded him to remove that competitor afterward. This contradicts the requirement of wisdom, so reflect on it.

The ninth: Ibrahim, peace be upon him, was granted Ishaq in old age, and granted Isma'il in his youth and vigor. It is customary that the heart is most attached to the firstborn children, and inclines to him most and loves him most, unlike one granted a child in old age. The position of a child after old age is like the position of desire for a woman.

The tenth: the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, used to take pride in saying:
"I am the son of the two sacrificed ones."
meaning his father Abdullah, and his grandfather Isma'il.

(Lataifa: on the station of khullah)

It is a station that admits no rivalry from anything other than the Beloved. The taking of a child is a branch among the branches of the heart. The Beloved was jealous over His intimate friend, lest there dwell in a branch of his heart something other than Him. So He commanded him to slaughter him. When he submitted in compliance, that rivalry departed and love was purified for its rightful owner. Then the glad tidings came: ﴿And We ransomed him with a tremendous sacrifice﴾.

The intent was not that he should be punished, but that he should be tested so as to be refined.

The wonder is not in the Friend's command to slaughter the son; the wonder is in his carrying out the slaughter with his own hand. Had it not been for total immersion in love of the command, such a command would not have been easy to bear. Therefore its traces were made a place of return for hearts, which yearn for them more intensely than birds yearn for their nests.

(Chapter)

Consider the state of our third father, Ibrahim, the imam of the upright ones (hunafa'), the shaykh of the prophets, the pillar of the world, and the Friend of the Lord of the worlds among the children of Adam.

Consider what his trial led to, his patience, and his giving of himself to God.

Consider how his giving of himself to God and his support of His religion led to God taking him as a khalil for Himself, and commanding His Messenger and Friend Muhammad (ﷺ) to follow his creed. I will point out to you one quality of the many things God honoured him with in his trial of slaughtering his son. God, blessed and exalted, rewarded him for surrendering his son to God's command by blessing his offspring and multiplying them until they filled the plain and the mountain. God, blessed and exalted, is not outdone in generosity by anyone, and He is the most generous of the generous.

Whoever leaves something for His sake, or does something for His sake, God gives him multiples of what he left of that thing, many times over, and rewards him with many times over what he did for His sake. When Ibrahim was commanded to slaughter his son, he hastened to obey God's command, and the son agreed with his father, out of mutual contentment and submission. God, knowing their truthfulness and fidelity, ransomed him with a tremendous sacrifice and gave them what He gave them of His bounty. Among some of His gifts was that He blessed their descendants until they filled the earth, for the purpose of having children is nothing but procreation and the multiplication of offspring. For this reason Ibrahim said: ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from the righteous﴾, and said: ﴿My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [also] from my descendants﴾.

The utmost of what he feared and dreaded from slaughtering his son was the cutting off of his line. When he gave his son to God, and the son gave himself, God multiplied his offspring for him, blessed them, and increased them until they filled the world, and He placed prophethood and the Book among his descendants exclusively, and brought forth from them Muhammad. It is mentioned that Dawud (peace be upon him) wished to know the number of the Children of Israel, so he commanded that they be brought together, and sent for that nuqaba' (leaders) and 'urafa' (overseers), and ordered them to report the count to him. They remained for a period unable to accomplish that. Then God revealed to Dawud: "You know that I promised your father Ibrahim, when he was commanded to slaughter his son and hastened to obey My command, that I would bless his descendants until they become equal to the stars. Make them such that their number cannot be counted. You wish to count a number that I have decreed cannot be counted." He mentioned the rest of the hadith. Thus He made from his line these two great nations whose number none can count but God, their Creator and Provider: the Children of Israel and the Children of Isma'il. Apart from this, God honoured him with the elevation of his mention and beautiful praise, on the tongues of all nations, and among the angels in the heavens. This is part of the fruit of his dealing with God. So woe to the one who knows Him and then deals with others: how losing his bargain is, and how great his regret.

[Section: The Perfection of Love]

Then khullah includes the perfection and ultimate end of love, such that no room remains in the heart for anything other than the beloved. It is a station that does not accept sharing in any way. This station is specific to the two Friends, may the prayers and peace of God be upon them both: Ibrahim and Muhammad, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "God has taken me as a khalil just as He took Ibrahim as a khalil."

In the Sahih, from him (ﷺ), he said: "If I were to take a khalil from among the people of the earth, I would have taken Abu Bakr as a khalil, but your companion is the khalil of God."

In another hadith: "I disavow before every khalil his khullah."

When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) asked for a child and was given one, and his love was attached to his heart, a branch was taken from it. The Beloved was jealous over His khalil that there should be a place in his heart for another, so He commanded him to slaughter him. The command was in a dream, so that carrying out the command would be a greater trial and test. The intent was not the slaughter of the child, but the slaughter of him from the heart, so that the heart would be purified for the Lord. When the Friend (peace be upon him) hastened to comply and placed the love of God above the love of his son, the aim was achieved, the slaughter was lifted, and he was ransomed with a tremendous sacrifice. For the Lord, exalted, never commanded something and then utterly annulled it; rather, He must leave some part of it or a substitute for it, just as He left the law of ransom, and just as He left the recommendation of charity before private conversation, and just as He left the five prayers after the fifty were removed and kept their reward, saying: "The word is not changed before Me: they are five in action and fifty in reward."

[Section: Love and Khullah]

As for what some of the confused think, that love is more perfect than khullah, and that Ibrahim is the khalil of God while Muhammad is the beloved of God, this is from their ignorance. For love is general and khullah is specific, and khullah is the ultimate end of love. The Prophet (ﷺ) informed that God took him as a khalil just as He took Ibrahim as a khalil, and he denied that he could have a khalil other than his Lord, while he informed of his love for Aisha, her father, Umar ibn al-Khattab, and others.

Also, God, glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed, God loves those who are constantly repentant and loves those who purify themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 222]. And ﴿God loves the patient﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 146]. And ﴿God loves the doers of good﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 148]. And ﴿God loves those who act justly﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 42]. The young repentant one is a beloved of God, but khullah is specific to the two Friends. This is only from a lack of knowledge and understanding of God and His Messenger (ﷺ).

(Chapter)

Khullah is the love that penetrates the spirit and heart of the lover until no place remains in it for anything other than the beloved, as it has been said:

"You have penetrated the path of the spirit within me, and for this the intimate friend was named khalil."

This is the secret for which—and God knows best—the Friend was commanded to slaughter his son, the fruit of his heart and the morsel of his liver. For when he asked for a son and was given one, a branch of his heart became attached to him. Khullah is a station that does not accept partnership or division. So the Friend was jealous over his khalil that there should be a place in his heart for another. He therefore commanded him to slaughter the son, to remove the rival from his heart.

When he prepared himself for that and resolved upon it with a firm resolve, the purpose of the command was achieved. There was no benefit left in taking the son's life, so He prevented it and ransomed him with a tremendous sacrifice. He was told: ﴿O Ibrahim, you have fulfilled the vision﴾ [al-Saffat: 104], that is, you acted as one who affirms it. ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good﴾ [al-Saffat: 80], We reward whoever hastens to obey Us, so We gladden his eye just as We gladdened your eye by your compliance with Our commands, and by preserving the son and his safety. ﴿Indeed, this was the clear trial﴾ [al-Saffat: 106]: it is the Beloved's testing of His lover, and His examining him so that he prefers His pleasure. Thus He perfects His blessings upon him; it is a trial of affliction and a gift of grace upon him together.

This call, to which only the special ones of His creation are summoned, and among them the people of intellect and insight, is not answered by everyone. Not every eye is comforted by it. Its people are those who are in the midst of the right hand's grasp on the day of the two graspings, and the rest of the people of the right hand are at its edges.

"Not every eye is comforted by the Beloved, nor does everyone who is called answer the caller."

"Whoever does not answer the caller of your guidance, leave him; he will answer everyone who has become a caller to error."

"And say to the inflamed eyes: beware of seeing the light of the sun, so cover yourself against the darkness of the nights."

"And forgive souls that did not give themselves to their beloved; leave them and what they chose, and do not be harsh."

[Section: The Drowning]

The Shaykh al-Islam said:

(Chapter of Drowning) God Most High said: ﴿So when they had both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead﴾ [al-Saffat: 103].

This is a term by which, in this chapter, is indicated one who has reached the middle of the station and passed the limit of separation.

The manner of his inference from the indication of the verse: when Ibrahim (ﷺ) and his son reached what they reached in hastening to comply and resolving to carry out the slaughter commanded, the father laid him upon his forehead at once, took the knife and swung it toward his throat. In that state he turned away from himself and his son, and passed away by God's command from them both. Thus he entered the sea of gathering of secret, heart, and concern upon God, and passed the limit of distinction that prevents compliance with this command.

His words: "﴿When they had both submitted﴾" means they surrendered and yielded to God's command, so there remained no dispute from either the father or the son, but pure submission and complete surrender.

His words: "﴿and he put him down upon his forehead﴾" means he threw him down upon his forehead, which is the side of the brow that faces the ground when one lies down, and that is the posture of one who is to be slaughtered.

His words: "he reached the middle of the station" he does not mean a specific station, and for this reason he left it indefinite and did not restrict it. The "station" among them is a stage of the stations of the wayfarers, and it differs according to its levels, and it has a beginning, a middle, and an end. The "drowning" referred to is to become in the middle of the station.

If it is said: drowning is more specific to the end of the station than to its middle, because it is immersion in it, such that it engulfs the heart and concern, so how does the Shaykh make it a middle in it?

I say: when the seeker's aspiration in this state is gathered upon the aim, and he turns away from all else, he has departed from the station of distinction and passed its limit into the station of gathering. He begins within the station, and the beginning of every station resembles the end of the one before it. When he reaches the middle of it, it engulfs his heart, concern, and will, just as one drowns who reaches the middle of a deep sea before arriving at its far shore.

(Section: That the Sacrifice Was Isma'il (peace be upon him))

Isma'il is the one who was sacrificed according to the correct view of the scholars among the Companions, the Successors, and those after them.

As for the claim that it was Ishaq, it is false for more than twenty reasons. I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya—may God sanctify his spirit—say: this view is only taken from the People of the Book, and it is even false by the text of their own book. For in it: God commanded Ibrahim to slaughter his son, his firstborn, and in one wording: his only son. The People of the Book, along with the Muslims, do not doubt that Isma'il is his firstborn. What deceived the proponents of this view is that in the Torah in their hands is: "Slaughter your son Ishaq." He said: this addition is from their distortion and lying, for it contradicts His saying: "Slaughter your firstborn and your only one." But the Jews envied the sons of Isma'il this honour and wished it to be theirs, and to bring it to themselves and claim it for themselves apart from the Arabs. But God refuses except to make His favour belong to its people. How could it be said that the sacrificed one was Ishaq, when God gave glad tidings to Ishaq's mother of him and of his son Ya'qub? God Most High said, speaking of the angels, that they said to Ibrahim when they brought him the glad tidings: ﴿Do not fear, for we have been sent to the people of Lut.—And his wife was standing, and she laughed, and We gave her glad tidings of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾ [Hud: 70–71]. It is impossible that He should give her the glad tidings that a child will be born to her and then command that he be slaughtered. And there is no doubt that Ya'qub (may God be pleased with him) is included in the glad tidings, so the glad tidings include Ishaq and Ya'qub in one wording, and this is the apparent meaning of the speech and its context.

If it is said: had the matter been as you have mentioned, "Ya'qub" would have been in the genitive as a conjunction with Ishaq, and the reading would be ﴿and after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾, that is, "and Ya'qub from after Ishaq".

It is said: the nominative does not prevent Ya'qub from being the one given glad tidings, because glad tidings are a specific speech, and it is the first true joyful report.

God's words: ﴿and after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾ [Hud: 71] is a sentence that includes these conditions, so it is glad tidings; indeed, the true reality of glad tidings is the declarative sentence.

And since glad tidings are speech, the position of this sentence is in the accusative by way of reporting after a verb of saying, as if the meaning is: "and We said to her: after Ishaq, Ya'qub." And the speaker, when he says, "I gave so-and-so glad tidings of the arrival of his brother and his family behind him," is understood by no one except as giving glad tidings of both matters together. This is what no person of understanding doubts at all. Then another matter weakens the genitive reading: the weakness of your saying, "I passed by Zayd and after him 'Amr," and because the conjunction stands in the place of the preposition, so it is not separated from the genitive, just as the preposition is not separated from the genitive.

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary on Surah 37, verses 102–107 (part 2 of 2):

And it is also indicated by the fact that when Allah, glorified is He, mentioned the story of Ibrahim and his son, the one who was sacrificed, in Surah (al-Saffat), He said: ﴿So when they both had submitted, and he put him down upon his forehead, And We called to him, "O Ibrahim, You have fulfilled the vision." Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good. Indeed, this was the clear trial. And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice. And We left for him among later generations: "Peace upon Ibrahim." Thus do We reward the doers of good. Indeed, he was among Our believing servants.﴾ [al-Saffat: 103–111].

Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿And We gave him the good news of Ishaq, a prophet from among the righteous.﴾ [al-Saffat: 112]. This is a good news from Allah, exalted is He, to him, as a reward for his patience in what he was commanded. This is very clear that the one given the good news of was other than the first, rather it is almost explicit in that.

If it is said: The second good news was about his prophethood, meaning that when the father was patient in what he was commanded, and the son submitted to the command of Allah, Allah rewarded him for that by granting him prophethood.

It is said: The good news was given regarding the whole: his very person and existence, and that he would be a prophet. That is why "nabiyyan" is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal muqaddar), meaning: "destined to be a prophet." So it is not possible to take the good news as referring to the essence and then restrict it to a subordinate circumstantial clause that functions like an adjunct; this is an absurd way of speaking. Rather, when the good news concerns his prophethood, then its concerning his existence is more fitting and more appropriate.

Also, there is no doubt that the one sacrificed was in Makkah, which is why the sacrifices on the day of sacrifice (yawm al-nahr) are performed there, just as the sa'i between al-Safa and al-Marwa and the stoning of the pillars (rami al-jimar) were prescribed as a reminder of the matter of Isma'il and his mother, and to keep alive the remembrance of Allah. It is well known that Isma'il and his mother were the ones who were in Makkah, not Ishaq and his mother. For this reason, the place and time of the sacrifice are connected to the Sacred House (al-Bayt al-Haram), whose building was shared by Ibrahim and Isma'il, and slaughtering in Makkah was part of the completion of the Hajj to the House, which was established by the hand of Ibrahim and his son Isma'il, in time and place. Had the sacrifice been in al-Sham, as the People of the Book claim and those who took from them maintain, then the sacrifices and the slaughter would have been in al-Sham and not in Makkah.

Also, Allah, glorified is He, named the one sacrificed "Halim" (forbearing), because none is more forbearing than one who submits himself to slaughter in obedience to his Lord. And when He mentioned Ishaq, He named him "'Alim" (knowing). He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Has there come to you the story of the honored guests of Ibrahim? When they entered upon him and said, "Peace." He said, "Peace, a people unknown."﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 24–25]

Up to His saying: ﴿They said, "Do not fear," and gave him good tidings of a knowing boy.﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 28]

This is Ishaq without doubt, because he was from his wife, and she was the one who was given the good news of him. As for Isma'il, he was from the concubine (suriyyah). Also, both of them were given the good news of him in old age and despair of having a child, whereas Isma'il was born before that.

Also, Allah, glorified is He, established the human custom that the firstborn is more beloved to the parents than those born after him. When Ibrahim, peace be upon him, asked his Lord for a child and He granted him one, a portion of his heart became attached to love for him. And Allah, exalted is He, had taken him as a close friend (khalil), and friendship (khullah) is a station that requires the singling out of the Beloved with love, and that no one else be made to share in it. So when the son took a portion of the father's heart, the jealousy of the friendship came to pull it out of the heart of the Khalil. So He commanded him to sacrifice the beloved. When he proceeded to sacrifice him, and the love of Allah was greater in his heart than the love of the son, the friendship was then purified of any admixture of partnership. Thus there remained no benefit in the slaughter, since the benefit lay in the resolve and the settling of the soul upon it. The purpose had been achieved, so the command was abrogated, the sacrificial son was ransomed, the Khalil confirmed the vision, and the Lord's objective was fulfilled.

It is known that this trial and test occurred with the first-born only, and it would not have occurred with another child apart from the first. Rather, in the other child there was no competition with the friendship that would call for a command to slaughter him. This is most evident.

Also, Sarah, the wife of the Khalil (ﷺ), was extremely jealous of Hajar and her son, for she was a slave-girl. When she bore Isma'il and his father loved him, Sarah's jealousy intensified, so Allah, glorified is He, commanded that Hajar and her son be taken away from her and settled in the land of Makkah, so that the heat of jealousy would cool from Sarah. This was from His mercy and compassion, exalted is He. How then would He command, after this, that her son be slaughtered while the son of the slave-girl is left as he is? This is with Allah's mercy toward her, the removal of harm from her, and His restoring her. How then would He command, after this, the slaughter of her son rather than the son of the slave-girl? Rather, His perfect wisdom required that He command the slaughter of the son of the concubine, so that the heart of the mistress would soften toward her and her son, and the harshness of jealousy would turn into mercy, and the blessing of this slave-girl and her son would become manifest to her, and that Allah does not waste a household of which this woman and her son are part. And so that He might show His servants His restoring after breaking, His gentleness after hardship, and that the outcome of the patience of Hajar and her son in distance, loneliness, strangeness and submission to the slaughter of the son, led to what it led to: making their traces and footsteps rites for His believing servants and acts of worship for them until the Day of Resurrection. This is His sunnah, exalted is He, toward whomever He wills to elevate among His creation: that He bestows favor upon him after his weakness, humiliation and brokenness. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We wished to confer favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them the inheritors.﴾ [al-Qasas: 5]

That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.

(Section)

And he said in Ighathat al-Lahfan, quoting Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah in his book "al-Jawab al-Sahih liman Baddala Din al-Masih":

He said: In their Torah, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, said to Ibrahim, peace be upon him: "Sacrifice your son, your firstborn, your only one, Ishaq," an addition by them to the wording of the Torah.

I say: This is definitively false from ten aspects.

The first: his firstborn and only son is Isma'il, by the consensus of the three faiths. So combining that he was commanded to sacrifice his firstborn with specifying him as Ishaq is combining two contradictories.

The second: Allah, glorified and exalted is He, commanded Ibrahim to move Hajar and her son Isma'il away from Sarah and settle them in the wilderness of Makkah, lest Sarah be upset. So He commanded the removal of the concubine and her son from her, preserving her heart and averting the harm of jealousy from her. How then would He, glorified and exalted is He, after this command the slaughter of Sarah's son and leave the concubine's son? This is something wisdom does not require.

The third: the story of the sacrifice was certainly in Makkah, and for this reason Allah made the slaughter of offerings and sacrifices in Makkah, as a reminder to the community of what happened between their father Ibrahim and his son.

The fourth: Allah, glorified is He, gave Sarah, mother of Ishaq, the good news: ﴿of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾ [Hud: 71]. So He gave her the good news of both together. How then would He, after that, command the slaughter of Ishaq, when He had given their parents the good news of the child of his child?

The fifth: when Allah, glorified and exalted is He, mentioned the story of the one sacrificed, and his surrender of himself to Allah, and Ibrahim's proceeding to sacrifice him, and finished his story, He said after it:
﴿And We gave him the good news of Ishaq, a prophet from among the righteous.﴾ [al-Saffat: 112].
So Allah gave thanks for his submission to His command and his offering of his son to Him, and made among his reward for that that He gave him Ishaq. Thus Isma'il was saved from the slaughter, and Ishaq was added to him.

The sixth: Ibrahim, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, asked his Lord for a child. Allah answered his supplication and gave him the good news, and when the boy reached the age of striving with him, He commanded him to sacrifice him. He said, exalted is He:
﴿And he said, "Indeed, I will go to my Lord; He will guide me. My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous." So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy.﴾ [al-Saffat: 99–101].
This is evidence that this child was given the good news after his supplication and his asking his Lord to grant him a child, and this one given the good news of is certainly the one commanded to be sacrificed, by the explicit text of the Qur'an.

As for Ishaq, he was given the good news without any supplication from him, rather in old age, and when someone like him could not have a child, and the good news of him was given to his wife Sarah. For this reason she marvelled at the birth of a child from her and him.

He said, exalted is He: ﴿And our messengers did come to Ibrahim with good tidings. They said, "Peace." He said, "Peace," and he did not delay to bring a roasted calf. But when he saw their hands not reaching toward it, he regarded them with suspicion and felt from them fear. They said, "Fear not; indeed, we have been sent to the people of Lut." And his wife was standing, and she laughed, so We gave her good tidings of Ishaq and after Ishaq, Ya'qub. She said, "Oh, woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and this, my husband, is an old man? Indeed, this is an amazing thing." They said, "Are you amazed at the command of Allah?"﴾

So reflect on the context of this good news and that, and you will find them to be two different good tidings, with different origins, one distinct from the other.

The first good news was to him. The second was to her.

The first good news is the one in which the one to be sacrificed was given the good news of, not the second.

The seventh: Ibrahim, peace be upon him, never brought Ishaq to Makkah at all, nor did he separate him from his mother. And how would Allah command him to take the son of his wife, to sacrifice him in the place of his co-wife in her land, and leave the son of his co-wife?

The eighth: when Allah took Ibrahim as a Khalil, friendship implies that his entire heart be attached to his Lord, with no portion of it left for another. When he asked for a child, He gave him Isma'il, and a portion of his heart became attached to him. So His Khalil, glorified is He, wanted that portion to be for Him alone, not for any other creature. So He tested him by commanding the slaughter of his son. When he proceeded to comply, that friendship was purified for Him, and became purely for Allah alone. So the command to slaughter was abrogated, since the purpose had been achieved, which was the resolve and the settling of the soul upon compliance.

It is known that this occurs with the firstborn, not with the last. When this purpose was achieved from the first child, there was no need for the same in the other child. For if the love of the other child had competed with the friendship, he would have been commanded to slaughter him as he commanded the first. And if the one commanded to be slaughtered had been the other child, then He would have permitted him, with the first, to compete with the friendship for a long period, and then commanded him to remove that competitor afterward. This contradicts the requirement of wisdom, so reflect on it.

The ninth: Ibrahim, peace be upon him, was granted Ishaq in old age, and granted Isma'il in his youth and vigor. It is customary that the heart is most attached to the firstborn children, and inclines to him most and loves him most, unlike one granted a child in old age. The position of a child after old age is like the position of desire for a woman.

The tenth: the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, used to take pride in saying:
"I am the son of the two sacrificed ones."
meaning his father Abdullah, and his grandfather Isma'il.

(Lataifa: on the station of khullah)

It is a station that admits no rivalry from anything other than the Beloved. The taking of a child is a branch among the branches of the heart. The Beloved was jealous over His intimate friend, lest there dwell in a branch of his heart something other than Him. So He commanded him to slaughter him. When he submitted in compliance, that rivalry departed and love was purified for its rightful owner. Then the glad tidings came: ﴿And We ransomed him with a tremendous sacrifice﴾.

The intent was not that he should be punished, but that he should be tested so as to be refined.

The wonder is not in the Friend's command to slaughter the son; the wonder is in his carrying out the slaughter with his own hand. Had it not been for total immersion in love of the command, such a command would not have been easy to bear. Therefore its traces were made a place of return for hearts, which yearn for them more intensely than birds yearn for their nests.

(Chapter)

Consider the state of our third father, Ibrahim, the imam of the upright ones (hunafa'), the shaykh of the prophets, the pillar of the world, and the Friend of the Lord of the worlds among the children of Adam.

Consider what his trial led to, his patience, and his giving of himself to God.

Consider how his giving of himself to God and his support of His religion led to God taking him as a khalil for Himself, and commanding His Messenger and Friend Muhammad (ﷺ) to follow his creed. I will point out to you one quality of the many things God honoured him with in his trial of slaughtering his son. God, blessed and exalted, rewarded him for surrendering his son to God's command by blessing his offspring and multiplying them until they filled the plain and the mountain. God, blessed and exalted, is not outdone in generosity by anyone, and He is the most generous of the generous.

Whoever leaves something for His sake, or does something for His sake, God gives him multiples of what he left of that thing, many times over, and rewards him with many times over what he did for His sake. When Ibrahim was commanded to slaughter his son, he hastened to obey God's command, and the son agreed with his father, out of mutual contentment and submission. God, knowing their truthfulness and fidelity, ransomed him with a tremendous sacrifice and gave them what He gave them of His bounty. Among some of His gifts was that He blessed their descendants until they filled the earth, for the purpose of having children is nothing but procreation and the multiplication of offspring. For this reason Ibrahim said: ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from the righteous﴾, and said: ﴿My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [also] from my descendants﴾.

The utmost of what he feared and dreaded from slaughtering his son was the cutting off of his line. When he gave his son to God, and the son gave himself, God multiplied his offspring for him, blessed them, and increased them until they filled the world, and He placed prophethood and the Book among his descendants exclusively, and brought forth from them Muhammad. It is mentioned that Dawud (peace be upon him) wished to know the number of the Children of Israel, so he commanded that they be brought together, and sent for that nuqaba' (leaders) and 'urafa' (overseers), and ordered them to report the count to him. They remained for a period unable to accomplish that. Then God revealed to Dawud: "You know that I promised your father Ibrahim, when he was commanded to slaughter his son and hastened to obey My command, that I would bless his descendants until they become equal to the stars. Make them such that their number cannot be counted. You wish to count a number that I have decreed cannot be counted." He mentioned the rest of the hadith. Thus He made from his line these two great nations whose number none can count but God, their Creator and Provider: the Children of Israel and the Children of Isma'il. Apart from this, God honoured him with the elevation of his mention and beautiful praise, on the tongues of all nations, and among the angels in the heavens. This is part of the fruit of his dealing with God. So woe to the one who knows Him and then deals with others: how losing his bargain is, and how great his regret.

[Section: The Perfection of Love]

Then khullah includes the perfection and ultimate end of love, such that no room remains in the heart for anything other than the beloved. It is a station that does not accept sharing in any way. This station is specific to the two Friends, may the prayers and peace of God be upon them both: Ibrahim and Muhammad, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "God has taken me as a khalil just as He took Ibrahim as a khalil."

In the Sahih, from him (ﷺ), he said: "If I were to take a khalil from among the people of the earth, I would have taken Abu Bakr as a khalil, but your companion is the khalil of God."

In another hadith: "I disavow before every khalil his khullah."

When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) asked for a child and was given one, and his love was attached to his heart, a branch was taken from it. The Beloved was jealous over His khalil that there should be a place in his heart for another, so He commanded him to slaughter him. The command was in a dream, so that carrying out the command would be a greater trial and test. The intent was not the slaughter of the child, but the slaughter of him from the heart, so that the heart would be purified for the Lord. When the Friend (peace be upon him) hastened to comply and placed the love of God above the love of his son, the aim was achieved, the slaughter was lifted, and he was ransomed with a tremendous sacrifice. For the Lord, exalted, never commanded something and then utterly annulled it; rather, He must leave some part of it or a substitute for it, just as He left the law of ransom, and just as He left the recommendation of charity before private conversation, and just as He left the five prayers after the fifty were removed and kept their reward, saying: "The word is not changed before Me: they are five in action and fifty in reward."

[Section: Love and Khullah]

As for what some of the confused think, that love is more perfect than khullah, and that Ibrahim is the khalil of God while Muhammad is the beloved of God, this is from their ignorance. For love is general and khullah is specific, and khullah is the ultimate end of love. The Prophet (ﷺ) informed that God took him as a khalil just as He took Ibrahim as a khalil, and he denied that he could have a khalil other than his Lord, while he informed of his love for Aisha, her father, Umar ibn al-Khattab, and others.

Also, God, glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed, God loves those who are constantly repentant and loves those who purify themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 222]. And ﴿God loves the patient﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 146]. And ﴿God loves the doers of good﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 148]. And ﴿God loves those who act justly﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 42]. The young repentant one is a beloved of God, but khullah is specific to the two Friends. This is only from a lack of knowledge and understanding of God and His Messenger (ﷺ).

(Chapter)

Khullah is the love that penetrates the spirit and heart of the lover until no place remains in it for anything other than the beloved, as it has been said:

"You have penetrated the path of the spirit within me, and for this the intimate friend was named khalil."

This is the secret for which—and God knows best—the Friend was commanded to slaughter his son, the fruit of his heart and the morsel of his liver. For when he asked for a son and was given one, a branch of his heart became attached to him. Khullah is a station that does not accept partnership or division. So the Friend was jealous over his khalil that there should be a place in his heart for another. He therefore commanded him to slaughter the son, to remove the rival from his heart.

When he prepared himself for that and resolved upon it with a firm resolve, the purpose of the command was achieved. There was no benefit left in taking the son's life, so He prevented it and ransomed him with a tremendous sacrifice. He was told: ﴿O Ibrahim, you have fulfilled the vision﴾ [al-Saffat: 104], that is, you acted as one who affirms it. ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good﴾ [al-Saffat: 80], We reward whoever hastens to obey Us, so We gladden his eye just as We gladdened your eye by your compliance with Our commands, and by preserving the son and his safety. ﴿Indeed, this was the clear trial﴾ [al-Saffat: 106]: it is the Beloved's testing of His lover, and His examining him so that he prefers His pleasure. Thus He perfects His blessings upon him; it is a trial of affliction and a gift of grace upon him together.

This call, to which only the special ones of His creation are summoned, and among them the people of intellect and insight, is not answered by everyone. Not every eye is comforted by it. Its people are those who are in the midst of the right hand's grasp on the day of the two graspings, and the rest of the people of the right hand are at its edges.

"Not every eye is comforted by the Beloved, nor does everyone who is called answer the caller."

"Whoever does not answer the caller of your guidance, leave him; he will answer everyone who has become a caller to error."

"And say to the inflamed eyes: beware of seeing the light of the sun, so cover yourself against the darkness of the nights."

"And forgive souls that did not give themselves to their beloved; leave them and what they chose, and do not be harsh."

[Section: The Drowning]

The Shaykh al-Islam said:

(Chapter of Drowning) God Most High said: ﴿So when they had both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead﴾ [al-Saffat: 103].

This is a term by which, in this chapter, is indicated one who has reached the middle of the station and passed the limit of separation.

The manner of his inference from the indication of the verse: when Ibrahim (ﷺ) and his son reached what they reached in hastening to comply and resolving to carry out the slaughter commanded, the father laid him upon his forehead at once, took the knife and swung it toward his throat. In that state he turned away from himself and his son, and passed away by God's command from them both. Thus he entered the sea of gathering of secret, heart, and concern upon God, and passed the limit of distinction that prevents compliance with this command.

His words: "﴿When they had both submitted﴾" means they surrendered and yielded to God's command, so there remained no dispute from either the father or the son, but pure submission and complete surrender.

His words: "﴿and he put him down upon his forehead﴾" means he threw him down upon his forehead, which is the side of the brow that faces the ground when one lies down, and that is the posture of one who is to be slaughtered.

His words: "he reached the middle of the station" he does not mean a specific station, and for this reason he left it indefinite and did not restrict it. The "station" among them is a stage of the stations of the wayfarers, and it differs according to its levels, and it has a beginning, a middle, and an end. The "drowning" referred to is to become in the middle of the station.

If it is said: drowning is more specific to the end of the station than to its middle, because it is immersion in it, such that it engulfs the heart and concern, so how does the Shaykh make it a middle in it?

I say: when the seeker's aspiration in this state is gathered upon the aim, and he turns away from all else, he has departed from the station of distinction and passed its limit into the station of gathering. He begins within the station, and the beginning of every station resembles the end of the one before it. When he reaches the middle of it, it engulfs his heart, concern, and will, just as one drowns who reaches the middle of a deep sea before arriving at its far shore.

(Section: That the Sacrifice Was Isma'il (peace be upon him))

Isma'il is the one who was sacrificed according to the correct view of the scholars among the Companions, the Successors, and those after them.

As for the claim that it was Ishaq, it is false for more than twenty reasons. I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya—may God sanctify his spirit—say: this view is only taken from the People of the Book, and it is even false by the text of their own book. For in it: God commanded Ibrahim to slaughter his son, his firstborn, and in one wording: his only son. The People of the Book, along with the Muslims, do not doubt that Isma'il is his firstborn. What deceived the proponents of this view is that in the Torah in their hands is: "Slaughter your son Ishaq." He said: this addition is from their distortion and lying, for it contradicts His saying: "Slaughter your firstborn and your only one." But the Jews envied the sons of Isma'il this honour and wished it to be theirs, and to bring it to themselves and claim it for themselves apart from the Arabs. But God refuses except to make His favour belong to its people. How could it be said that the sacrificed one was Ishaq, when God gave glad tidings to Ishaq's mother of him and of his son Ya'qub? God Most High said, speaking of the angels, that they said to Ibrahim when they brought him the glad tidings: ﴿Do not fear, for we have been sent to the people of Lut.—And his wife was standing, and she laughed, and We gave her glad tidings of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾ [Hud: 70–71]. It is impossible that He should give her the glad tidings that a child will be born to her and then command that he be slaughtered. And there is no doubt that Ya'qub (may God be pleased with him) is included in the glad tidings, so the glad tidings include Ishaq and Ya'qub in one wording, and this is the apparent meaning of the speech and its context.

If it is said: had the matter been as you have mentioned, "Ya'qub" would have been in the genitive as a conjunction with Ishaq, and the reading would be ﴿and after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾, that is, "and Ya'qub from after Ishaq".

It is said: the nominative does not prevent Ya'qub from being the one given glad tidings, because glad tidings are a specific speech, and it is the first true joyful report.

God's words: ﴿and after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾ [Hud: 71] is a sentence that includes these conditions, so it is glad tidings; indeed, the true reality of glad tidings is the declarative sentence.

And since glad tidings are speech, the position of this sentence is in the accusative by way of reporting after a verb of saying, as if the meaning is: "and We said to her: after Ishaq, Ya'qub." And the speaker, when he says, "I gave so-and-so glad tidings of the arrival of his brother and his family behind him," is understood by no one except as giving glad tidings of both matters together. This is what no person of understanding doubts at all. Then another matter weakens the genitive reading: the weakness of your saying, "I passed by Zayd and after him 'Amr," and because the conjunction stands in the place of the preposition, so it is not separated from the genitive, just as the preposition is not separated from the genitive.

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary on Surah 37, verses 102–107 (part 2 of 2):

And it is also indicated by the fact that when Allah, glorified is He, mentioned the story of Ibrahim and his son, the one who was sacrificed, in Surah (al-Saffat), He said: ﴿So when they both had submitted, and he put him down upon his forehead, And We called to him, "O Ibrahim, You have fulfilled the vision." Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good. Indeed, this was the clear trial. And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice. And We left for him among later generations: "Peace upon Ibrahim." Thus do We reward the doers of good. Indeed, he was among Our believing servants.﴾ [al-Saffat: 103–111].

Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿And We gave him the good news of Ishaq, a prophet from among the righteous.﴾ [al-Saffat: 112]. This is a good news from Allah, exalted is He, to him, as a reward for his patience in what he was commanded. This is very clear that the one given the good news of was other than the first, rather it is almost explicit in that.

If it is said: The second good news was about his prophethood, meaning that when the father was patient in what he was commanded, and the son submitted to the command of Allah, Allah rewarded him for that by granting him prophethood.

It is said: The good news was given regarding the whole: his very person and existence, and that he would be a prophet. That is why "nabiyyan" is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal muqaddar), meaning: "destined to be a prophet." So it is not possible to take the good news as referring to the essence and then restrict it to a subordinate circumstantial clause that functions like an adjunct; this is an absurd way of speaking. Rather, when the good news concerns his prophethood, then its concerning his existence is more fitting and more appropriate.

Also, there is no doubt that the one sacrificed was in Makkah, which is why the sacrifices on the day of sacrifice (yawm al-nahr) are performed there, just as the sa'i between al-Safa and al-Marwa and the stoning of the pillars (rami al-jimar) were prescribed as a reminder of the matter of Isma'il and his mother, and to keep alive the remembrance of Allah. It is well known that Isma'il and his mother were the ones who were in Makkah, not Ishaq and his mother. For this reason, the place and time of the sacrifice are connected to the Sacred House (al-Bayt al-Haram), whose building was shared by Ibrahim and Isma'il, and slaughtering in Makkah was part of the completion of the Hajj to the House, which was established by the hand of Ibrahim and his son Isma'il, in time and place. Had the sacrifice been in al-Sham, as the People of the Book claim and those who took from them maintain, then the sacrifices and the slaughter would have been in al-Sham and not in Makkah.

Also, Allah, glorified is He, named the one sacrificed "Halim" (forbearing), because none is more forbearing than one who submits himself to slaughter in obedience to his Lord. And when He mentioned Ishaq, He named him "'Alim" (knowing). He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Has there come to you the story of the honored guests of Ibrahim? When they entered upon him and said, "Peace." He said, "Peace, a people unknown."﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 24–25]

Up to His saying: ﴿They said, "Do not fear," and gave him good tidings of a knowing boy.﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 28]

This is Ishaq without doubt, because he was from his wife, and she was the one who was given the good news of him. As for Isma'il, he was from the concubine (suriyyah). Also, both of them were given the good news of him in old age and despair of having a child, whereas Isma'il was born before that.

Also, Allah, glorified is He, established the human custom that the firstborn is more beloved to the parents than those born after him. When Ibrahim, peace be upon him, asked his Lord for a child and He granted him one, a portion of his heart became attached to love for him. And Allah, exalted is He, had taken him as a close friend (khalil), and friendship (khullah) is a station that requires the singling out of the Beloved with love, and that no one else be made to share in it. So when the son took a portion of the father's heart, the jealousy of the friendship came to pull it out of the heart of the Khalil. So He commanded him to sacrifice the beloved. When he proceeded to sacrifice him, and the love of Allah was greater in his heart than the love of the son, the friendship was then purified of any admixture of partnership. Thus there remained no benefit in the slaughter, since the benefit lay in the resolve and the settling of the soul upon it. The purpose had been achieved, so the command was abrogated, the sacrificial son was ransomed, the Khalil confirmed the vision, and the Lord's objective was fulfilled.

It is known that this trial and test occurred with the first-born only, and it would not have occurred with another child apart from the first. Rather, in the other child there was no competition with the friendship that would call for a command to slaughter him. This is most evident.

Also, Sarah, the wife of the Khalil (ﷺ), was extremely jealous of Hajar and her son, for she was a slave-girl. When she bore Isma'il and his father loved him, Sarah's jealousy intensified, so Allah, glorified is He, commanded that Hajar and her son be taken away from her and settled in the land of Makkah, so that the heat of jealousy would cool from Sarah. This was from His mercy and compassion, exalted is He. How then would He command, after this, that her son be slaughtered while the son of the slave-girl is left as he is? This is with Allah's mercy toward her, the removal of harm from her, and His restoring her. How then would He command, after this, the slaughter of her son rather than the son of the slave-girl? Rather, His perfect wisdom required that He command the slaughter of the son of the concubine, so that the heart of the mistress would soften toward her and her son, and the harshness of jealousy would turn into mercy, and the blessing of this slave-girl and her son would become manifest to her, and that Allah does not waste a household of which this woman and her son are part. And so that He might show His servants His restoring after breaking, His gentleness after hardship, and that the outcome of the patience of Hajar and her son in distance, loneliness, strangeness and submission to the slaughter of the son, led to what it led to: making their traces and footsteps rites for His believing servants and acts of worship for them until the Day of Resurrection. This is His sunnah, exalted is He, toward whomever He wills to elevate among His creation: that He bestows favor upon him after his weakness, humiliation and brokenness. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We wished to confer favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them the inheritors.﴾ [al-Qasas: 5]

That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.

(Section)

And he said in Ighathat al-Lahfan, quoting Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah in his book "al-Jawab al-Sahih liman Baddala Din al-Masih":

He said: In their Torah, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, said to Ibrahim, peace be upon him: "Sacrifice your son, your firstborn, your only one, Ishaq," an addition by them to the wording of the Torah.

I say: This is definitively false from ten aspects.

The first: his firstborn and only son is Isma'il, by the consensus of the three faiths. So combining that he was commanded to sacrifice his firstborn with specifying him as Ishaq is combining two contradictories.

The second: Allah, glorified and exalted is He, commanded Ibrahim to move Hajar and her son Isma'il away from Sarah and settle them in the wilderness of Makkah, lest Sarah be upset. So He commanded the removal of the concubine and her son from her, preserving her heart and averting the harm of jealousy from her. How then would He, glorified and exalted is He, after this command the slaughter of Sarah's son and leave the concubine's son? This is something wisdom does not require.
